report.source_text: Laparoscopy demonstrated an SB mass adherent within the pelvis. Adhesiolysis was performed through a lower midline laparotomy to allow an oncological, stapled, side-to-side, antiperistaltic SB resection. The SB lumen was significantly narrowed by the mass, and multiple enlarged, firm mesenteric lymph nodes were palpable. There was no evidence of metastatic disease.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 80-year-old man presented to the emergency department with symptoms of small bowel obstruction (colicky abdominal pain, obstipation, nausea, vomiting). A CT abdomen/pelvis revealed a large, obstructing distal small bowel mass that had increased in size compared to a previous scan. Surgical intervention involved laparoscopy, adhesiolysis, and a stapled side-to-side antiperistaltic small bowel resection. Intraoperatively, the small bowel lumen was significantly narrowed, and enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes were palpable. Histopathology of the resected specimen confirmed a 75 mm grade 2 jejunal leiomyosarcoma with negative margins and metastatic disease in one of four resected lymph nodes. Other lymph nodes showed features consistent with known lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, and EBV-associated leiomyosarcoma was excluded. The patient recovered well and was discharged on postoperative day 7. A multidisciplinary meeting recommended ongoing surveillance.
